title: Overload
fullDescription: CyberPower UPS beeps rapidly and flashes overload indicator when load surpasses rating. Output may shut off to protect UPS.

title: Battery bad
fullDescription: Sealed lead-acid batteries last 3-5 years. CyberPower detects capacity loss and flags for replacement.

fixSteps.title: Identify battery model
fixSteps.instruction: Check sticker or manual for RB number.

fixSteps.title: Install battery
fixSteps.instruction: Unscrew cover, swap battery, reconnect leads.

faq.a: Work with same voltage/Ah; avoid counterfeits.

title: Site wiring fault
shortDescription: Building outlet has missing ground or reversed polarity.
fullDescription: Protection from surges requires proper grounding. UPS detects wiring faults via outlet sensor.
videoSearchQuery: CyberPower UPS site wiring fault fix

title: Building wiring fault
fullDescription: Indicates larger building electrical problem, not just outlet. Neutral and ground should be near 0V; large difference means fault.

title: Low battery
shortDescription: Battery level near depletion during outage.
fullDescription:
After running on battery for some time, UPS signals imminent shutdown.

Save work and allow graceful shutdown via PowerPanel software.

faq.a: Use PowerPanel for automatic graceful shutdown.

title: Replace battery
shortDescription: Battery reached end of life — replace now.
fullDescription: Same as Battery Bad — time to swap for new CyberPower RB pack or equivalent sealed lead-acid battery.

title: Output off
fullDescription: Manually turned off or after fault. Press power button to enable.
videoSearchQuery: CyberPower UPS output off turn on

title: Overvoltage
fullDescription:
AVR (Automatic Voltage Regulation) units correct within range; beyond limits UPS switches to battery.

Check with voltmeter; persistent overvoltage is utility issue.

fixSteps.title: Contact utility
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent, report to electric company.

title: Undervoltage
fullDescription: Brownouts trigger AVR boost or battery mode. Chronic undervoltage may be utility or shared load issue.

faq.a: Not with UPS; AVR and battery protect.

title: Frequency error
shortDescription: Input frequency not in UPS tolerance.
fullDescription:
UPS expects 50/60Hz within narrow tolerance. Generator or inverter mains can drift causing errors.

UPS will stay on battery until input valid.

faq.a: Yes for dirty power — always conditions output.
